newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke - 3.0 pct not "knockout" for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke - 3.0 pct not "knockout" for EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Friday that the EMU entry target of three percent for budget deficit to GDP should not be seen as a "knockout" criterion for countries wishing to join the single currency in 1999.

"Contrary to the impression that is often raised in Germany 3.0 percent is not a knockout criterion for participation in monetary union," Welteke said in a prepared speech for delivery at an EMU conference.
To join Europe's planned currency union at its scheduled 1999 start, nations must meet strict entry criteria, including the three percent budget deficit target.

Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel however, has stressed the three percent limit in the Maastricht Treaty should be 3.0 percent precisely, and that Germany, although struggling to pare its deficit, would meet that.

Welteke, who is also president of the state central bank in Hesse, said he considered the numerical target problematic statistically and in terms of methodology, adding such targets were economically difficult to justify.
